scope.description: Bound measurement at the shipped default event capacity: does an unconsumed event stream park nodes and stall the cluster when the capacity is left at 1024?
assumptions: in-process 3-node cluster, majority quorum, in-process transport under harness control
only node 1 consumes its event stream; nodes 2 and 3 leave the handle's receiver unread
writes are paced at one per millisecond so consecutive decided-index changes are observed in separate ticks
excluded: deployments whose clients always drain events
any latency claim about how long a real cluster needs to reach 1024 transitions

basis.prefix: Same in-process 3-node cluster and actor setup as the executed revision (real OmniPaxos instances over MemoryStorage warmed by omnipaxos_runtime actors spawned with spawn_actor and a harness-local tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; one delivery task per node forwards outgoing messages to the receiver's handle_incoming). The new case drains events only on node 1 and leaves the default capacity in place (RuntimeConfig::default().event_capacity = 1024), then paces ordinary writes from the elected leader (one proposal per millisecond, 4000 proposals) so that the two unread nodes keep observing transitions until they reach the bound; it waits up to 90s for both to stop answering commands, then measures whether the healthy node 1 can still decide: it emits CA_EVENT default_capacity_parked_cluster {event_capacity,nodes_parked,decided_before,decided_after,append_notify_timeout_reached} and asserts that both unread nodes parked, that node 1 stayed responsive, that its decided index was unchanged across the attempt, and that at least 1024 transitions had been observed before the two nodes parked (so the bound really was the default rather than a smaller configured one).

before.description: Consequence probe: what the rest of the cluster loses when a majority of nodes' actors are parked by unconsumed event streams.
assumptions: 3 nodes, majority quorum 2; only node 1 consumes its event stream
same in-process transport and error-free memory storage as the other cases
event_capacity 8 on all nodes so the bound is reached quickly
excluded: any claim that a deployment reaches the bound in a given time

after.description: Bound measurement at the shipped default event capacity: does an unconsumed event stream park nodes and stall the cluster when the capacity is left at 1024?
assumptions: in-process 3-node cluster, majority quorum, in-process transport under harness control
only node 1 consumes its event stream; nodes 2 and 3 leave the handle's receiver unread
writes are paced at one per millisecond so consecutive decided-index changes are observed in separate ticks
excluded: deployments whose clients always drain events
any latency claim about how long a real cluster needs to reach 1024 transitions

prefix.before: Three real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2,3) over MemoryStorage, each driven by a real omnipaxos_runtime actor from spawn_actor with a harness-local tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; one in-process transport task per node forwards outgoing messages to the receiver's handle_incoming. RuntimeConfig: tick_period 2ms, egress_period 1ms, append_notify_timeout 1500ms; case 1/2 use event_capacity 64, case 3 uses 8. ServerConfig: election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1. Case 3 subscribes and drains events only on pid 1; pids 2 and 3 leave the receiver the handle owns unread, so after enough observed transitions their event channels fill and their actors park. It keeps paced ordinary writes coming from the elected leader, waits until two of the three nodes stop answering commands, then requires: node 1 still answers; node 1's `append_notify_with_timeout(_, 300ms)` resolves with Timeout (its own actor runs, so that endpoint is reachable) rather than Ok; node 1's decided index is unchanged one second later. It emits CA_EVENT parked_majority_cluster {nodes_parked,healthy_node_responsive,append_notify_timeout_reached,decided_before,decided_after}.
prefix.after: Same in-process 3-node cluster and actor setup as the executed revision (real OmniPaxos instances over MemoryStorage warmed by omnipaxos_runtime actors spawned with spawn_actor and a harness-local tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; one delivery task per node forwards outgoing messages to the receiver's handle_incoming). The new case drains events only on node 1 and leaves the default capacity in place (RuntimeConfig::default().event_capacity = 1024), then paces ordinary writes from the elected leader (one proposal per millisecond, 4000 proposals) so that the two unread nodes keep observing transitions until they reach the bound; it waits up to 90s for both to stop answering commands, then measures whether the healthy node 1 can still decide: it emits CA_EVENT default_capacity_parked_cluster {event_capacity,nodes_parked,decided_before,decided_after,append_notify_timeout_reached} and asserts that both unread nodes parked, that node 1 stayed responsive, that its decided index was unchanged across the attempt, and that at least 1024 transitions had been observed before the two nodes parked (so the bound really was the default rather than a smaller configured one).

revision_reason: Adds one case (`default_capacity_event_bound_stops_actor_loop`) and changes nothing else in the harness. The three existing cases are unchanged; the new case uses `RuntimeConfig::default()` unchanged (event_capacity 1024) to measure whether the park and the cluster-level stall also occur at the shipped default rather than only at the 64/8 bounds witnessed so far, which is currently a stated limitation argued from source.
